body:
# id(attestation): `sign_genesis` / `sign_claim` never check the signer is a player — a non-player's signed genesis or claim is dead on arrival, and signing succeeds silently

## Summary

`pkgs/id/src/attestation.rs` enforces its authority rules in the viewer: `compute_state` (attestation.rs:258) counts a genesis only when *each of the agreement's two players* has signed the identical agreement, and counts a claim only when its author is one of those players ("Claims answering a different agreement, **from non-players**, or with an outcome other than … are ignored", attestation.rs:254-255). The signing entry points enforce only one viewer invariant — `sign_genesis` (attestation.rs:171) refuses a duplicate-seat agreement, mirroring the viewer's malformed-agreement rule from #2863. Neither signer checks the other authority rule:

- `sign_genesis` never checks that the signing key is one of `agreement.players`. A third party can sign the agreement and produce a well-formed `attestation.genesis` event that no viewer will ever count toward the genesis pair.
- `sign_claim` (attestation.rs:208) never checks that the signing key is one of the players of the agreement the claim answers (it cannot check from the claim alone — see acceptance criteria for the shape this implies).

So a caller holding the wrong key — the realistic failure: a harness or wallet layer selects the wrong identity, or an operator signs with a witness/service key — gets a successful signature, a chain event, and an event id to hand out, and the object simply never exists for any viewer. That is the same failure shape closed for currency in #6422 ("creation reports success, consumption silently ignores") and for artifacts in #5623: a signed object should be refused at creation when the module's own consumption rules make it unreachable, so the mistake surfaces where the caller can fix it.

## Evidence (verified this run, origin/main `a2b4345e80`)

- Code: `sign_genesis` (attestation.rs:171-205) checks only `first == second` (duplicate seat) before serializing and calling `chain::sign`; `sign_claim` (attestation.rs:208-232) performs no check at all. `compute_state`'s genesis rule (`agreement.players.iter().all(|player| genesis.iter().any(|(author, signed)| author == player && …))`) and per-player claim collection (`author == player`) make non-player objects unreachable by construction.
- Probe (laptop, worktree of origin/main at `a2b4345e80`, `~/git/fleet/probe-attestation-wt`, integration test `pkgs/id/tests/probe_attestation_sign.rs`, `cargo test -p id --test probe_attestation_sign -- --nocapture`, 1 passed): `sign_genesis` by a third key naming neither seat → **Ok** (event produced); `sign_claim` by the same third key → **Ok**; `compute_state` over both players' genuine genesis events plus only the stranger's claim → **Proposed** (the stranger's claim is ignored, exactly as documented). Controls in the same probe: both players' sign calls succeed, and the existing duplicate-seat refusal errors as documented.

## Why it matters

The attestation PoC's own module doc states the principle: "Reconstruction is admission, not deserialization: derive conclusions from signature-verified authors and compare claims with the selected agreement. Reject, ignore, or dispute inconsistent input according to the API's rules; **never silently repair it or let an input's own claims establish authority**." The viewer side honors that; the signer side is the remaining half. This module is explicitly the shape later production attestation APIs would be built on (#2039 design, epic #2056 review gate), so the sign-side contract should be settled while it is still a PoC surface. The duplicate-seat refusal in `sign_genesis` already establishes the house shape: viewer invariants that make an object meaningless are refused at sign time with a typed `SignError`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `sign_genesis` refuses to sign when the signing key's `player_id` is not one of `agreement.players`, surfacing a typed `SignError` variant (e.g. `NotAPlayer`); no event is produced.
- [ ] `sign_claim` gains a way to refuse a non-player signer — e.g. it takes the `GenesisAgreement` (or its player set) alongside the claim, or a sibling checked entry point is added and the unchecked one is crate-private/test-only, mirroring the `sign_unchecked` pattern in artifact.rs. The chosen shape is the fixer's call; the requirement is that the public signing path cannot silently produce a claim no viewer will count.
- [ ] Tests: a non-player genesis signing and a non-player claim signing both error; both players' genuine genesis + claim flow still computes `Agreed` (the existing `attestation_poc.rs` demonstration passes unchanged).
- [ ] `compute_state` behavior is unchanged: non-player objects from other/legacy signers are still ignored, never counted.
- [ ] Out of scope: the witness slot (present and unused by design in this PoC) and objection handling (#2038/#2039).

## Notes

- Related: #2863 (duplicate-seat: the sign-time refusal precedent in this same function), #2868 (claim outcome domain, viewer side), #6422 (the currency sign-side validation gap — same failure shape, different module and rule; complementary, not a duplicate), #5623 (artifact sign-side precedent), #2898 (the reconstruction-is-admission design epic this module's doc cites).
- Found by Lane B (new-issue-creator-code-b), weighting away from Lane A's recent fleet-config/queue filings and Lane B's own recent dead-test and currency filings.
